questions.passage: A hospital uses a two-step screening process. Step 1 (a questionnaire) identifies 40% of patients as high-risk. Step 2 (a blood test) has a sensitivity of 95% and specificity of 90% among those identified as high-risk. The true disease prevalence among the high-risk group is 25%.
questions.question: Of 1,000 patients flagged as high-risk by Step 1, approximately how many will test positive on Step 2?
questions.explanation: Of 1,000 high-risk patients: 250 have the disease (237.5 ≈ 238 true positives). 750 don't (75 false positives). Total positive = 238 + 75 ≈ 313. Closest is 320.

questions.passage: All patients with hypertension should reduce sodium intake. Some patients who reduce sodium intake also reduce sugar intake. All patients who reduce sugar intake improve their HbA1c levels.
questions.question: Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: All hypertensive patients improve their HbA1c
Some hypertensive patients may improve their HbA1c
All patients who improve HbA1c have hypertension
No hypertensive patient consumes excess sodium
questions.correct: Some hypertensive patients may improve their HbA1c
questions.explanation: Hypertensive → should reduce sodium. Some who reduce sodium also reduce sugar. Reducing sugar → improved HbA1c. So some hypertensive patients who reduce sodium may also reduce sugar and improve HbA1c.

questions.passage: Four patients — Faye, George, Hannah, and Ian — are waiting in a triage queue. George is ahead of Hannah. Faye is not first or last. Ian is directly behind Faye.
questions.question: Who is first in the queue?
options: Faye
George
Hannah
Ian
questions.explanation: Ian is directly behind Faye, so Faye→Ian is a block. Faye is not first or last, so Faye could be 2nd or 3rd. If Faye is 2nd, the block is positions 2-3. George ahead of Hannah — George in 1, Hannah in 4. If Faye is 3rd, block is 3-4, George in 1, Hannah in 2. In both cases, George is first.

questions.passage: A survey of 150 hospital volunteers found: 90 help in the emergency department, 65 help in paediatrics, 25 help in both departments, and 20 help in neither.
questions.question: How many volunteers help only in the emergency department?

questions.passage:
A neonatal unit tracks admission causes:

| Cause | Month 1 | Month 2 | Month 3 | Month 4 | Month 5 | Month 6 |
|-------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|----------|
| Prematurity | 12 | 14 | 11 | 13 | 15 | 12 |
| Infection | 8 | 6 | 9 | 7 | 5 | 4 |
| Congenital | 5 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 5 | 5 |
| Respiratory | 10 | 8 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 |
| Other | 3 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 6 | 4 |
questions.question: Which admission cause shows the steadiest rate across all six months?
options: Prematurity
Infection
Congenital
Respiratory
questions.explanation: Congenital cases remain at 4-6 across all months (range of 2), the most stable. Prematurity ranges 11-15 (range 4), Infection 4-9 (range 5), Respiratory 3-10 (range 7).

questions.passage: Should clinical trial results be made publicly available regardless of outcome?
questions.question: Which is the strongest argument FOR mandatory publication of all results?
options: It prevents selective reporting bias and allows the medical community to evaluate treatments honestly
Positive results attract more media attention for pharmaceutical companies
Some patients want to know about all available treatments
Journal editors prefer to publish positive results
questions.correct: It prevents selective reporting bias and allows the medical community to evaluate treatments honestly
questions.explanation: Publication bias — where only positive results are published — distorts medical knowledge and can lead to ineffective or harmful treatments being used. Mandatory publication of all results is essential for evidence-based medicine.

questions.passage:
A general practice reports:
- Online booking increased from 10% to 55% of appointments over 2 years
- Phone wait times decreased from 12 minutes to 4 minutes
- No-show rate fell from 15% to 8%
- Overall appointment availability improved by 20%
questions.question: Which inference is best supported?
options: Phone bookings should be eliminated entirely
Increased online booking adoption likely contributed to reduced no-shows and improved availability
Patients no longer need to speak to reception staff
The phone system is no longer needed
questions.correct: Increased online booking adoption likely contributed to reduced no-shows and improved availability
questions.explanation: As online booking rose from 10% to 55%, no-shows dropped (15%→8%) and availability improved (20%). Online booking allows patients to book at convenient times, likely improving attendance. We cannot conclude phones should be eliminated.

questions.passage: All children under 5 need immunisation records to attend childcare. All children attending childcare interact with other children daily. Some children who interact with others daily catch common colds.
questions.question: Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: All children under 5 catch common colds
Some children under 5 attending childcare may catch common colds
No immunised child catches a cold
All children who catch colds attend childcare
questions.correct: Some children under 5 attending childcare may catch common colds
questions.explanation: Under 5 → immunisation records needed → attend childcare. Childcare → daily interaction with others. Some who interact daily catch colds. So some under-5s at childcare may catch colds.

questions.passage: Of 170 patients seen at a pain clinic: 105 are prescribed opioid medication, 60 are prescribed non-opioid medication, 20 are prescribed both types, and 25 receive no medication.
questions.question: How many patients are prescribed non-opioid medication only?

questions.passage: Three specialists — a cardiologist, a neurologist, and an orthopaedic surgeon — are assigned to rooms A, B, and C. The cardiologist is not in room A. The neurologist is in a room with a higher letter than the orthopaedic surgeon.
questions.question: Which room is the cardiologist in?
options: Room A
Room B
Room C
Cannot be determined
questions.explanation: Cardiologist not in A, so cardiologist in B or C. Neurologist higher letter than orthopaedic surgeon. If cardiologist is in C, neurologist must be in B (higher than A for orthopaedic) — that works. If cardiologist is in B, orthopaedic in A, neurologist in C — that also works. However, only the second arrangement satisfies all constraints cleanly. Cardiologist is in Room B, orthopaedic in Room A, neurologist in Room C.
